composed_rule: head = [[outer + 0x788] + 0x620]; the head is dereferenced without a null check
key = the stack string 'BlockCache' (10 bytes, SSO: pointer rsp + 0x10, length 10, NUL at rsp + 0x1a)
for trial in 1..8 over nodes n0..n7: handler = [vtable(n) + 0x38]; if handler != 0x4f8da10, return handler(n, key)
otherwise hit = helper(n, key) via 0x52f5290; if hit != 0, return hit
on a helper miss before the eighth trial: n = next(n) via vtable slot +0x88; if n is null, return 0

on a helper miss at the eighth trial: return walker(n7, key) via 0x514ba10, which steps to next(n7) first and repeats the same handler/helper rule without bound, returning 0 when it reaches a null node
every return path disposes the stack key string (_M_dispose, a no-op for this SSO string) and checks the stack canary

arguments.rsi: key string object (pointer at +0x0, length at +0x8)

helper.return_convention: the matching record's +0x20 first qword, or 0 when no record matches
helper.scope_note: bound by RE-001-chain-walk-dispatch-94; cited here as a callee only, not re-claimed

inferred: the names 'handler' for vtable slot +0x38 and 'next' for vtable slot +0x88, from their roles (dispatch target and chain step); no source-level class or function name is claimed
that the eight inline trials cover nodes n0..n7 and the walker covers n8 onward, because the walker steps to the next node before its first trial
that the 'BlockCache' bytes are a lookup key, from the stack string being passed unchanged to every helper call and every handler call
observed: every branch target, call target, vtable offset, GOT slot, relocation, FDE range, carve SHA and census in this file, each re-derived from the binary by verify.py
the key bytes 42 6c 6f 63 6b 43 61 63 68 65 ('BlockCache') materialized at rsp + 0x10 with length 10
the sentinel address 0x4f8da10 loaded by the lea at 0x514e55e, matching the walker packet's sentinel function address
unknowns: the source-level identity of the outer object, the chain nodes, the handlers, and the record payloads
what a handler result or a helper hit means to the four callers; both are returned verbatim, not interpreted
the behavior when the head node is null: the binary dereferences it without a guard, so no return value is claimed for that case
